correctness.rationale: Arc conflicts exactly identify the two-rail ladder independence complex (rungs and rails). Each symmetry orbit complex is explicitly computed for even and odd ladder lengths, yielding actual geometric fixed-point homeomorphisms. Signed simplicial Lefschetz fixes integer action signs on rank-one integral homology because Proposition 2.2 supplies an integral sphere. Finite-group rational averaging gives the quotient criterion; all boundary cases n>=2 addressed. Exact independent brute-force subset enumeration verifies the conflict graphs and involutions through n=10, full Betti vectors through n=7, and Lefschetz traces through n=9. Computational evidence is corroborative only.

originality.rationale: The nearest source settles nonequivariant homotopy only. Closest equivariant reports have different graph families (circular ladders and bidirected polygons) or different complexes (strong Morse matching complexes). Their full relevant results were read and compared at statement-and-implication level; none covers all three geometric fixed-point spaces, integral path action and rational quotient threshold. Absolute bibliographic priority remains uncertain.
residual_risks: An unindexed independent derivation or a less visible appendix may contain an equivalent open-ladder symmetry calculation.
The broader source arXiv:2608.30601 was inspected at abstract/main-result level rather than every appendix; this is not asserted as a whole-paper exclusion.
Only specified Klein-four actions and rational quotient homology are established; integral quotient torsion is not analyzed.

value.rationale: The exact fixed-polyhedron identifications are structural and uniform in path length; one involution is free, while the other two have different shorter-path fixed spaces. The all-n rank-one integral character and exact mod-eight rational quotient threshold answer natural symmetry questions invisible to the already-known sphere dimension, not merely a finite table or restatement of a standard reduction.
